ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure; on the left there is a four-membered carbon ring (cyclobutane, drawn as a diamond/square), and on the right a side chain extends from one carbon on the ring; the side chain is connected in sequence to a nitrogen-containing fragment N=N, then connected to O, and the O is labeled with H2 and a positive charge. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: Count only bonds between non-hydrogen atoms, and count single bonds, double bonds, and triple bonds all as one bond connection in the structure. The four-membered carbon ring itself has 4 C-C bonds. The side-chain portion has: 1 bond from the ring carbon to the external carbon, 1 bond from the external carbon to N, 1 bond for N=N, and 1 bond for N-O. The O-H bonds are not counted, because the problem requires excluding bonds involving hydrogen. Therefore the total is 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8.

method.method_draft: Read the instruction to count all non-hydrogen bonds and disregard arrows. From the image, count the four C-C bonds forming the cyclobutane ring. Then count the side-chain heavy-atom bonds: ring carbon to the exocyclic carbon, exocyclic carbon to N, N=N, and N-O. Add these visually enumerated bond groups: 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8.

method.method_draft: Read the prompt as asking for non-H heavy-atom bonds only. Convert the image into a heavy-atom graph: 4 ring carbons + 1 side-chain carbon + 2 N atoms + 1 O atom = 8 heavy atoms.
